title: Use visualizations to make a signal obvious

blocks.content:
Picture this. A teammate builds a dashboard for the fleet of servers you both watch, and every panel on it is a line chart. The data is all there, but three questions are difficult to answer. How close is that disk to full? Where do response times cluster? Where in the world is the traffic coming from?

A panel runs a query, then draws the result. A chart is one way to draw it. Grafana has many more. A gauge shows how close a disk is to full, a heatmap shows where values cluster, and a map shows data by location. The same data, drawn differently, makes a different point.

In this guide you'll tour a gallery of working examples.

Open the **Visualization Examples** dashboard.

It contains working examples of the visualizations Grafana can draw, including the three that answer your questions.
That's the gallery. It's a page of tiles, each linking to a working example of one visualization.
Next, look at the three visualizations that answer your three questions.

Find **Gauges**.

A gauge shows how far a number is from its limit at a glance. That's the disk question. Full is the limit, and the needle shows the distance left.
blocks.tooltip: This visualization shows the distance to a limit in one look, like a disk filling up or a queue near overflow.

blocks.content:
Find **Heatmaps**.

A heatmap shows where values cluster over time. That's the response-time question. Most requests land in a band, and you can see the band move when something changes.
blocks.tooltip: Dense spots mean many measurements landed there. Good for spotting patterns a line would hide.

blocks.content:
Click **Geomap**.

It opens working maps that plot data by location. That's the traffic question. The map draws each measurement where it happened, so busy regions stand out.
blocks.tooltip: Real data, real coordinates, drawn on a map.

blocks.content: Three questions, three visualizations. The gallery is where you saw them, but dashboards are where you'll use them. When your data arrives in Grafana Cloud, you pick the visualization that fits what you need to see, and it lives on a dashboard alongside the rest of what you watch. The [guide on dashboards](https://interactive-learning.grafana.net/guides/get-started-see-dashboards) shows you how to read one.
